entries.label: r4c1
entries.name: cell MLP + learned cell-to-action map
entries.hypothesis: No spatial convolutions. A deep per-cell MLP computes whether each cell is a good landing spot. A full learned linear map (K*Y*X to n_place) assigns those scores to action indices, so the net works under any permutation of observation cells or action indices. It uses less compute than the starting net, lr 2e-3, 2 epochs. Refuted if train and dev success stay at 0. That would point to the reward or dynamics rather than the action mapping.

entries.label: r4c3
entries.name: Deep trunk + mask + anti-collapse
entries.hypothesis: A residual trunk of four 3x3 convs (9x9 receptive field), the legality mask as input, and a 3x3 local logit head that can learn anchor shifts. Recipe: 3 epochs, gamma 0.9, lambda 0.85, entropy 0.02, and a DONE head that starts at zero with an offset of minus 2. This tests the anti-collapse idea on a network with more context and the misalignment hedges. Refuted if it stays at 0 while the other anti-collapse candidates score.

entries.label: r4c3
entries.name: Dilated trunk with global broadcast
entries.hypothesis: Replaces the 5x5-receptive-field trunk with residual 3x3 convs at dilations 1, 2 and 4, plus a pooled global vector added back to every cell, all with per-cell LayerNorm. Each placement score and the DONE decision can then use whole-grid context: what is still missing, and which supports exist elsewhere. Refuted if both seeds stay at 0, which would mean limited receptive field is not the bottleneck.

entries.label: r4c1
entries.name: Symmetry-mixture head + mask input
entries.hypothesis: Inputs gain the action mask (reshaped into per-type maps) and coordinate channels. A 5x5 output conv produces per-type logit maps for 5 variants (identity, flip-y, flip-x, rotate-180, transpose), which are summed. Training can strengthen whichever variant matches this world's action convention, and the 5x5 kernel covers anchor offsets. Recipe as r1c1. If a hidden layout mismatch is the blocker, success should rise above 0. A score of 0 refutes the idea.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: r3c3 with wider row/col channels
entries.hypothesis: Widen the circular row/column convolutions from 24 to 40 channels in the front end and from 20 to 28 in the deep block. Undoing the X/2 shift for every target, missing and height channel needs roughly one output channel per shifted input channel, so 24 ReLU channels may be a bottleneck for exact per-layer alignment. Compute rises to about 1.8x. Refuted if the mean is at or below 0.46.

entries.label: r2c3
entries.name: half-roll, 128 envs, 2 epochs
entries.hypothesis: Same as the 128-env candidate, but with 2 PPO epochs instead of 4. The fixed compute then buys about 1.8 times more fresh samples (about 225k steps, about 110 updates). Fresh designs may matter more than reusing samples when every episode has a new target. Refuted if it scores clearly below the 4-epoch 128-env candidate, meaning sample reuse is worth more than sample count here.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: best + 2 PPO epochs
entries.hypothesis: Same as r2c1, but ppo_epochs is 2. The budget gives about 1.86x more environment steps (about 243k, roughly 118 updates), with total gradient steps about the same as r2c1. Fresh, less reused data should cut overfitting to stale rollouts and expose the agent to more designs. Refuted if dev success is at or below 0.90, which would mean reusing each sample more is worth more than seeing more data.

entries.label: r4c3
entries.name: Best + gamma 0.95
entries.hypothesis: Change: r3c2 with gamma raised from 0.9 to 0.95, a smaller step than r3c1's 0.97 and with lambda unchanged. Why: the agent presses DONE with tall stacks unfinished, and a moderately longer horizon makes the +1 exact-build bonus worth more. It should not destabilise training the way 0.97 seemed to (r3c1 seeds: 0.61 and 0.15). Refuted if it scores below r3c2's 0.58 by more than the noise, or if the seeds split widely again.

entries.label: r4c1
entries.name: r3c2 + lr 1e-3
entries.hypothesis: Training is limited by samples and updates (about 77 updates, success still rising). Raising lr from 7e-4 to 1e-3 lets each of those updates move further, and the linear decay to zero keeps late training stable. Expect dev success above 0.90 with no collapse. Refuted if dev success is at or below about 0.88, or a seed collapses, which would mean the larger step makes training unstable.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: x roll + more updates, lr 1.5e-3
entries.hypothesis: Same network as r3c1. The recipe uses n_envs 128 (2048 samples per update, so about twice as many updates), 32 minibatches of 64 and lr 1.5e-3. Fresher data, about twice the gradient steps and a higher learning rate should speed learning, since r3c1 was still improving at the end. Refuted if dev success is at or below 0.80, or it collapses to DONE because steps are too large.

entries.label: r3c2
entries.name: r1c2 + 2 epochs at 128 envs, ent 0.02
entries.hypothesis: Change: r1c2's network with 2 PPO epochs instead of 3. The batch stays at 128 envs and 2048 samples, and the entropy coefficient rises to 0.02. That gives about 227k samples and 111 updates instead of 157k and 77. r2c2 collapsed to DONE with 64 envs. The larger batch and extra entropy should stop that early collapse while keeping the gain from more samples. Refuted if a seed collapses to DONE or dev success is not above 0.89.

entries.label: r4c1
entries.name: half-roll, ent_coef 0.003
entries.hypothesis: Same as r1c1, with ent_coef cut from 0.01 to 0.003. The policy already places almost every cell correctly (IoU 0.99). The remaining failures are small order or placement errors, and the entropy bonus may slow commitment to the exact best action. Evaluation is greedy, so a sharper policy should help. Expect dev success above 0.89. A drop below 0.85, or a seed stuck early, would refute this by showing the bonus was needed for exploration.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: r3c3 + n_envs 64
entries.hypothesis: Same as r3c3, but with 64 parallel worlds and 8 minibatches of 128 samples. The policy then updates about 120 times instead of 60, on fresher data, with the same samples and gradient steps. Its seed-0 run was ahead early (0.25 training success at 25% of training, against about 0.02 for r3c3), and the global context in the head may make use of that speed. Refuted if 2-seed dev success is below about 0.87.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: r3c1 + entropy 0.05
entries.hypothesis: Same as r3c1, but ent_coef rises from 0.03 to 0.05, the upper bound. Going from 0.01 to 0.03 raised both seeds (0.80 to 0.83 mean). A stronger pull towards uniform should keep DONE unlikely for longer and keep exploring placement orders. Greedy evaluation is not hurt by a slightly flatter policy. Refuted if the mean falls below about 0.80 because the policy stays too random (lower training success at 100%), or a seed collapses.

entries.label: r4c1
entries.name: r3c1, n_envs 64 (4x updates)
entries.hypothesis: Same as r3c1 but with n_envs 64 and n_minibatches 8. Samples, minibatch size (128) and gradient steps stay the same, but there are about 154 updates instead of 77. Going from 38 to 77 updates helped (0.81 → 0.85, with tight seeds), so even fresher data should get the agent away from DONE faster and give more time for exact builds. Refuted if the mean is at or below 0.85, or a seed falls below 0.75.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: circ head + 2x more updates
entries.hypothesis: Same network and recipe as r3c2, except n_envs 128 and n_minibatches 16. Minibatches stay at 128 samples, and the total number of samples is unchanged. That gives twice as many PPO updates, and twice the learning-rate decay steps, on the same data. r3c2's training success was still climbing at the end, which suggests too few updates rather than too little data. Refuted if dev success is at or below 0.33, or if it collapses to DONE.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: Soft-capped logits, max entropy
entries.hypothesis: If the policy collapses early, for example to an early DONE or to one wrong placement habit, exploration never finds an exact build. Soft-capping the logits (8*tanh(l/8)) bounds how deterministic the policy can become. Entropy is set to 0.05, the bound and above anything tried, and gamma to 0.99. The base is the dual-head GN net. Refuted if training and dev success stay 0.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: r3c3 with cap 4
entries.hypothesis: This is r3c3 with the soft cap raised from 3 to 4. Caps of 2 and 2.5 scored 0 and cap 3 scored 1/512, so a looser cap may let the policy sharpen enough on correct placements for greedy builds to be exact more often. Refuted if dev stays 0, which would point to cap 3 or luck.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: r3c6 + 32 minibatches
entries.hypothesis: Change: n_minibatches 32 (64 samples each) instead of 16, which doubles the gradient steps on the same data. Why: the agent is under-optimised; in r3c4, 32 minibatches with 16-step rollouts scored about the same as 16 minibatches (0.64 vs 0.67), so this is safe to pair with full-episode rollouts. Refuted if it scores clearly below r3c6.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: r3c1 with 64 minibatches
entries.hypothesis: The only change from r3c1 is 64 minibatches of 64 samples instead of 32, which doubles the Adam steps on the same fresh samples at no extra compute. The 1-epoch run failed, which suggests the agent is short of optimisation steps. Refuted if dev success is clearly below 11% or drops to 0.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: D4 late-mirror head
entries.hypothesis: Mirrors after local features rather than before. A centred symmetric convolution first computes 32-channel footprint features from the full trunk features. The 8 D4 copies of those rich local features are then mixed by a 1x1 layer into per-type logits. Each logit can then read full local evidence at its mirrored positions, not just 8 reduced channels, which should fit a flipped or transposed action layout better. Refuted if dev and training success are both 0.

entries.label: r4c3
entries.name: Anchor-free primary head net
entries.hypothesis: New idea: if the described anchor is wrong, the fixed-footprint pool head gives misplaced features and noise. Its slow dense path wastes parameters. This net drops both. A wider residual trunk (48 channels) feeds a per-type nonlinear head (1x1 to 24 hidden channels, then a grouped 5x5) as the only placement path, with small output init. Slow DONE, the per-action bias and r3c3's recipe are kept. Refuted if it scores at or below 0.090.

entries.label: r3c2
entries.name: Conv head plus layout-free residual
entries.hypothesis: This world may not match its description, for example in action-index layout or DONE position. If so, conv heads would map logits to the wrong actions. This adds a zero-initialised dense Linear over flattened conv features to all n_actions logits (DONE included). It can fix any index mismatch, and the conv prior is kept where the layout is right. Recipe: orthogonal init, 2 epochs, lr 2e-3. Refuted if both seeds stay at 0.

entries.label: r4c3
entries.name: Fourier positions fed into head
entries.hypothesis: This is r3c2, the only trial to score (0.35), with extra position input. Sine and cosine position channels are added at the input, and the position channels are also concatenated into the pooling head. Positional cues were what made r3c2 learn, so giving the head position directly should make that learning more reliable and narrow the gap between seeds (0.15 vs 0.54). Refuted if the mean is at or below r3c2's 0.35.

entries.label: r4c4
entries.name: Two-sided symmetry kitchen sink
entries.hypothesis: Hedges on both sides at once: the obs under all 8 symmetries, 8 output and mask layouts, both DONE positions, circular padding, GroupNorm and global context. Trains with 1 PPO epoch, entropy 0.01 and gamma 0.95. If several deviations are present together (an obs-group misalignment plus an action-layout or edge deviation), each single-change run fails, but this one could leave zero. Refuted if training success stays 0.

entries.label: r4c3
entries.name: norm+critic, 4x more updates
entries.hypothesis: This is candidate 1 with 32 minibatches of 64 samples instead of 8 of 256, and lr 1e-3. That gives 4x more gradient steps at the same FLOPs, because FLOPs are charged per sample, not per update. It targets a world harder than described, where learning stalls before the first exact build within this budget. If it scores 0, an optimisation-speed bottleneck is refuted.

entries.label: r2c1
entries.name: 16-layout mask, default recipe
entries.hypothesis: Extends the four-layout design to 16 layouts: type-major and position-major indexing, each in (y,x) or (x,y) axis order, each under all 4 flip combinations. The mask goes in under all 16, and 16 per-type output maps are put back into those layouts and summed. If this world indexes actions position-major or with a 180° rotation, only this broader hedge can align the mask with the grid. Refuted if both seeds score 0 and late training success is 0.

entries.label: r1c1
entries.name: mask4-layout baseline
entries.hypothesis: This rebuilds the only family that scored above 0. The legal mask goes in under 4 index layouts plus coordinates, followed by a 1x1 stem and a residual 3x3 trunk. Per-type logit maps are re-laid in the same 4 layouts and summed, so the network can learn how this world maps action indices to cells. I expect a dev score of at least 0.1. If both seeds score 0, this world breaks its description beyond flips and transposes.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: r3c1 with a deeper trunk and global context
entries.hypothesis: This adds a third GroupNorm residual 3x3 block. Before it, pooled global features (mean and max) are projected and added back to every cell. Exact builds need a wider view: the 2x2 landing heights, nearby target structure, and how far the build has progressed. Compute is about 1.3x, so the trial gets about 100k steps. Refuted if dev success is at or below r3c1's 0.003.

entries.label: r1c1
entries.name: Four-layout mask net (reproduction)
entries.hypothesis: A faithful reproduction of the only family that has ever scored. The mask goes in as channels under four layouts (identity, transposed, y-flip, x-flip), plus coordinate channels. A 1x1 stem feeds a residual 3x3 trunk. Per-type logit maps are re-laid in the same four layouts and summed, so the network can learn whichever action indexing the world really uses. Compute ratio is about 1, so it gets the full step budget. If both seeds score 0 on dev, this world's deviation is not one of these four layouts.

entries.label: r1c2
entries.name: mask8 dihedral layout net
entries.hypothesis: This uses the same net with all 8 symmetries of the square (dihedral layouts): the identity, the transpose, and every flip of each, for both the mask inputs and the output maps. Worlds have deviated in different ways, so covering every flip and transpose should catch a rot180 or transpose+flip mismatch that the 4-layout set misses. It is still about as cheap as the starting net. Refuted if it scores below the 4-layout net, or 0 on both seeds while the 4-layout net scores above 0.

entries.label: r3c1
entries.name: Four-layout net, 4x more updates
entries.hypothesis: Same network as r1c1 (the only trial with nonzero training success). The recipe changes to n_envs 64 and 16 minibatches, so the same 131k steps give 128 PPO updates instead of 32. With so few updates, PPO may stop long before the policy learns the precise fill decisions an exact build needs. If both seeds still show 0 training and 0 dev success, update count is not the bottleneck.

entries.label: r1c2
entries.name: mask 8-layout dihedral
entries.hypothesis: Same network, but the mask input and the output maps use all 8 combinations of transpose, y-flip and x-flip (4 flips if the grid is not square). This covers rotations and double flips that the 4-layout version cannot express, at almost the same compute. If it beats the replica, this world uses a layout outside the 4. It is refuted if it scores 0 while the replica scores above 0, or if both score 0.

entries.label: r2c2
entries.name: Dihedral layouts with DONE-first offset
entries.hypothesis: This world may put DONE at index 0 and shift every placement by one, which the earlier layout hedges cannot catch. This net covers both offsets (DONE last, and DONE first with placements shifted), each over 8 type-major dihedral layouts, with one DONE head per offset. If it learns where the plain 8-layout net scored 0, the indices are shifted. If both seeds score 0, an offset is not the deviation.

entries.label: r4c3
entries.name: Global-context trunk on r3c2 recipe
entries.hypothesis: Uses r3c3's global-board-context bias inside the residual block, trained on r3c2's 61-update recipe. On the 30-update recipe, global context scored 0.0195 against 0.0146, and both of its seeds were above 0.01. Knowing the board-wide progress should help with build order and with stopping at the right time, at almost no extra FLOPs. Expect dev above 0.038. Refuted if dev is at or below 0.038.

entries.label: r4c2
entries.name: D4 head, 2 epochs
entries.hypothesis: Same layout-agnostic network as candidate 1. The recipe uses 2 PPO epochs and ent_coef 0.01, giving about 236k steps with more sample reuse and exploration. The extra exploration may help find the correct layout group and complete builds before the policy sharpens. Success where candidate 1 fails favours sample reuse. Zero for both points away from a layout mismatch and toward a reward or dynamics difference.

entries.label: r4c5
entries.name: circular sym8 LN tyx+yxt
entries.hypothesis: The circular dilated trunk (receptive field covers the whole torus) with obs symmetries, LayerNorm stems and trunk, gain-0.01 outputs, and type-major plus type-minor action orders summed. This targets a rolled obs combined with mis-scaled inputs or a type-minor action order; the plain circular net may miss such stacked deviations. A score of 0.05 or more while the plain circular net scores 0 means the extra fixes are needed. A 0 for both refutes the roll hypothesis.

entries.label: r1c2
entries.name: Frames x centred window x orders
entries.hypothesis: One shared centred (2K-1) window conv produces type maps for every frame. Each map is flattened both type-major and anchor-major, and a ×5 softmax picks among them. This covers anchor-offset and flattening-order mismatches as well as frame transforms. A small dense term from the global vector is added. The idea is refuted if this scores 0 while candidate 1 scores above 0. That would mean the window and order options only cost samples.

entries.label: r2c1
entries.name: Frames x 3 orders x DONE position
entries.hypothesis: This extends the r1c2 window head to 48 options: 8 frames × 3 index orders (t-y-x, y-x-t, y-t-x) × DONE last or first. Each option gets its own map, and a ×5 softmax starting uniform picks one. If DONE is at index 0 or the type sits in the middle of the index, the agent cannot stop cleanly, which would explain zero training success. Refuted if both seeds score 0 on training and dev.

entries.label: r3c1
entries.name: Per-type soft cell permutation
entries.hypothesis: Each type slot's map is passed through a learned row-softmax cell permutation P[T,YX,YX]. P starts at zero logits, so the mix is uniform. This covers any per-type anchor scramble, roll, stride or offset with 16k weights instead of r2c3's 131k-weight remap, which is kept as a fallback. If the anchors are scrambled within each type, this should clearly beat 0.018 on both seeds. Scores ≤0.02 refute a per-type cell remap.

entries.label: r2c3
entries.name: 48 layouts + learned dense action map
entries.hypothesis: Change: candidate 1's head plus a gain-0.01 learned linear map from a 4-channel 1x1 projection of the spatial features to every action, including DONE. This can learn any fixed action permutation, such as compact per-type indexing. Why: it is a catch-all if the layout is non-geometric. Refuted if it scores no higher than candidate 1. If both score 0, the problem lies outside action layout (observation or dynamics).

entries.label: r2c4
entries.name: Hybrid: DONE-frame mix + cell attention
entries.hypothesis: This sums the 32-candidate frame × order × DONE-position window mixture and the per-action cell-attention head, both at gain 0.01, on a width-32 trunk. The structured candidates can lock on quickly if the layout is a shifted or dihedral one, and the attention head catches any unstructured remainder. Expect a score at least as high as the better of candidates 1 and 2, with a higher minimum seed. If it trails both, combining the heads makes credit assignment harder, and round 3 should keep only one.

entries.label: r1c2
entries.name: Frames x centred window x 2 orders
entries.hypothesis: The mismatch may combine a dihedral remap, an anchor-corner offset and anchor-major flattening. A shared centred 3x3 (2K-1) window conv outputs per-frame type maps. Each map is re-indexed into its frame and flattened both type-major and anchor-major (16 components, ×5 softmax). A gain-0.01 dense term comes from the global vector. Dev above 0 here while candidate 1 stays at 0 would point to an anchor offset or ordering mismatch. All 0 refutes it.

entries.label: r1c1
entries.name: 8-frame dihedral pooled head
entries.hypothesis: The world swaps the documented action layout for a dihedral one. Footprint-pooled logits are computed once and re-indexed into 8 frames, each with its own 1x1 output, and a x5 softmax picks the frame. With r≈0.94 this costs no samples. Prediction: dev well above 0, with the frame weights concentrating. Refuted if both training and dev stay at 0, which would mean the mismatch is not dihedral, or if dev sits at about 0.078, which would mean a collapse.

entries.label: r3c3
entries.name: circular trunk + 2D cyclic roll head
entries.hypothesis: The trunk and window convs use circular padding. The frame-mixed type maps then pass through a learned full-grid circular conv (T→T, kernel Y×X), so any 2D wrap-around shift of the anchor grid, combined with dihedral frames and type relabelling, can be represented. A softmax picks between the 2 flatten orders. If the observation is also rolled, the circular padding keeps the true neighbourhoods. It is refuted if train and dev are both 0.

notes.B: g3 not written: all 9 attempts (3 runs) were over the 1,000-word limit (1,019-1,250 words), so B's final is its last kept program, g2 (departure decided by the user, 16 Nov 2026)

changes.change: Header changed from 4 rounds x 3 candidates x 2 seeds to 4 x 6 x 1. This tests twice as many distinct ideas per search.
changes.evidence: All 84 two-seed trials, the starting architecture and every seed scored exactly 0. The second seed never disagreed with the first, so it added no information. The 4-seed retrain still guards against a lucky single seed.

changes.change: Added a compact list of idea families that have already scored 0, with an instruction not to re-run them alone.
changes.evidence: Searches 1 to 7 each independently re-tested 1-2 epoch recipes, per-layer heads, transformers and layout-free heads, and all of them scored 0 every time.

changes.change: Replaced 'half refine the current best, one change each' with: while every score is 0, stack several compatible untried fixes per candidate, and ablate only after a nonzero result.
changes.evidence: Single-change ablation pairs, such as 1 vs 2 epochs or head A vs head B, all came out 0 vs 0, so they could not tell anything apart. Refining a 0-scoring 'best' was meaningless in every search.

changes.change: Added a short list of directions no earlier search tried, labelled as unverified: init and normalisation hygiene, factorised logits, lr 3e-3, lambda 0.99, rollouts covering a full episode, and raw-input skips into the head.
changes.evidence: No logged trial used small-gain policy init, orthogonal init, LayerNorm or GroupNorm in a conv trunk, lr above 2e-3, or factorised type+anchor logits.

changes.change: Added a rule for what to do after a nonzero result: concentrate the remaining rounds on variants of it, including a near-copy to test robustness.
changes.evidence: A search can only beat the starting architecture by selecting a trial that scores above 0. Every one of the 7 searches selected the starting architecture.

changes.change: Added engineering notes: read sizes from spec, keep r at or below about 1.5, and per-layer B*Z reshapes cost about 2-3x the time.
changes.evidence: Per-layer nets took 210 to 237 s, against 40 to 110 s for 2D nets. Future worlds have other sizes, so time scales with Z. No trial failed, so the current caps are safe.

changes.change: Rewrote the summary of what is known. Matching the hidden action layout is now the main finding, and generic fixes are listed as having failed in every world.
changes.evidence: World 1 had 0 in all 6 non-frame trials and 0.37 to 0.91 in every frame-mixture trial. World 6 had 0 in every trial without the transposed head, and every trial with it scored. Worlds 2, 3, 5 and 7 had 72 zeros across all generic families.

changes.change: Round 1 is now a sweep of layout hypotheses: each candidate tests a different layout hypothesis with separate learnable heads, on a common base that worked.
changes.evidence: Both solves came from layout heads found in round 2, after round-1 generic stacks scored 0. Starting with these heads should save a round.

changes.change: Advise separate heads per hypothesis with a mixture that can commit (frame logits scaled by 5), not zero-initialised scalar gates on shared logits.
changes.evidence: Separate per-frame heads scored 0.51 to 0.91, and scaling frame logits by 5 gave 0.81 against 0.51. Additive gates scored 0 in world 2 r4c3 and world 4 r2c2, and only 0.04 in world 4 r4c2.

changes.change: Added layout hypotheses not yet tested: flattening-order mixtures with separate heads, anchor-corner mixtures, type-permutation mixtures, and products of these with frames.
changes.evidence: World 4 scored above 0 only once flattening-order and flip gates were added. Worlds 2, 3, 5 and 7 stayed at 0 under frame and transpose heads, which suggests a different misalignment.

changes.change: Gave concrete recipes for use after a nonzero result. One is 2 epochs, lr 1.5e-3, 16 minibatches. The other, for r≤1, is 1 epoch, 128x64, 64 minibatches, lr 3e-3, gamma 0.995. Also advise pruning unused hypothesis heads to free samples.
changes.evidence: World 1: 2 epochs beat 3 (0.87 against 0.51), and lr 1.5e-3 gave 0.91. World 6: lr 3e-3 with 64 minibatches gave 0.97, and the transposed-only head (r 0.91, 426k samples) gave 0.96.

changes.change: Added a warning about seed noise: one 0 or a low score next to a nonzero sibling does not refute the idea, and deeper trunks have not helped.
changes.evidence: Near-copies scored 0.87 against 0.25 and 0.44 against 0.15. Adding a third conv scored 0.48 and 0.37, against 0.51 to 0.87 for the base.

changes.change: Shortened the list of failed families and merged in the families that failed under g1. Kept the header at 4x6x1.
changes.evidence: The g1 header produced both solves, found in round 2. The program must stay under 1,000 words.

changes.change: Header changed from 4x6x1 to 3 rounds x 4 candidates x 2 seeds. Candidates are judged by the mean and the minimum over the 2 seeds, and designs with high scores on both seeds are preferred.
changes.evidence: Search bests averaged about 0.96, but the picks retrained on 4 seeds averaged 0.789. Collapses are bimodal (11 runs at exactly 0.078). Seed fragility is now the largest loss, and one seed per candidate cannot detect it.

changes.change: Every candidate now starts on a default recipe: 2 epochs, 128x16, 32 minibatches, gamma 0.97, lambda 0.95, ent 0.005, lr 1.5e-3.
changes.evidence: The 2-epoch recipe raised matched designs from 0.1-0.2 to 0.8-0.95 in four worlds (2, 5, 6, 7). 32 minibatches helped in worlds 3 and 6 and was neutral elsewhere. lr 1.5e-3 sits in the middle of the per-world best range (1e-3 to 3e-3).

changes.change: Round 1 now tests only frame-based heads: footprint-pooling frames; frames x centred window x 2 orders plus a dense term; identity+transposed square heads; and a per-type frame mixture at scale 2.
changes.evidence: These four families cover the winning layout in all 7 worlds. Frame mixtures won worlds 2, 4, 5 and 7, frames with windows and orders won worlds 1 and 3, and identity+transposed won world 6. Non-frame heads alone scored 0 in every world.

changes.change: Added a collapse diagnosis: train ≈ dev ≈ 0.078 marks a degenerate attractor, not partial progress.
changes.evidence: 11 runs in worlds 1, 3, 6 and 7 scored exactly 0.0781, with matching training success.

changes.change: Added to the failed list: 1-epoch recipes, gamma 0.99 or more, 64-env batches, index rolls, 5x5 windows, mixture scale 10 and non-frame layout heads alone.
changes.evidence: 1 epoch failed in 6 of 7 worlds. Gamma 0.99 collapsed worlds 5 and 7 (0.15, 0.078). 64 envs hurt in worlds 2, 5 and 7. Rolls and 5x5 windows scored about 0 in world 3. Scale 10 was neutral in worlds 1 and 5.

changes.change: Advise r ≤ 1 and batched or einsum per-frame heads rather than grouped convs.
changes.evidence: Slimming to r ≤ 1 raised samples and scores in worlds 2, 4 and 7. Grouped convs were charged about 1.8 against about 1.25 by hand in worlds 2, 4 and 6.

changes.change: Header changed from 4x3x2 to 4 rounds x 6 candidates x 1 seed, which tests twice as many distinct ideas.
changes.evidence: Every non-success was an exact 0 on both seeds, so the second seed added no information. In world 2 the hit was nonzero on both seeds of both recipes, so one seed is enough to detect a hit. Selection noise is limited because the final score is retrained on 4 seeds anyway.

changes.change: Added the world-2 reference net and recipe, and made it a mandatory round-1 candidate, together with wider layout hedges.
changes.evidence: World 2 r4c1/r4c2 reached 0.22 while the unhedged control r4c3 scored 0 on the same recipe. In 6 worlds, hedges were tried only in rounds 3 to 4.

changes.change: No recipe-only or capacity-only candidates while all scores are 0.
changes.evidence: More than 30 recipe and capacity variants across 7 worlds never moved a zero.

changes.change: Told the search to avoid slow layout-free heads and zero-initialised or softmax gating, and to sum hedged components at full scale.
changes.evidence: Dense remaps, flat MLPs and attention heads failed in worlds 1 and 3 to 7. The summed full-scale hedge succeeded in world 2.

changes.change: Told the search not to hard-code footprints, anchors, channel meanings or grid sizes, and to read sizes from spec.
changes.evidence: The successful net never used spec.footprints or channel slicing. Hand-shaped heads failed everywhere, and grid sizes will vary.

changes.change: Added escalation steps for when zeros persist (dynamics, obs channel order, action count) and refinement steps once there is a hit.
changes.evidence: Worlds 1 and 3 to 7 stayed at zero even under the hedges tried, so their deviation is still unknown. World 2's hit was never refined.

changes.change: Round 1 now tests two complementary 4-layout sets (A: identity, transpose, y-flip, x-flip; B: the other 4 grid symmetries), each with and without obs-symmetry input, plus LayerNorm variants. The 16-layout, 5x5, DONE-index and dense candidates are dropped.
changes.evidence: 4-layout sums scored in worlds 1, 2, 6 and 7. 16- and 24-layout sums scored 0 in nearly every world. DONE-index hedges never helped (they matched the reference in worlds 1, 2 and 6). Obs symmetries were essential in worlds 1 and 5. LayerNorm was the only escape in world 4.

changes.change: Round 2 must split the scoring hedge into all 4 of its single layouts, keeping its other components.
changes.evidence: Single correct layouts scored 0.80-0.94 in worlds 1, 2, 6 and 7, against 0.15-0.37 for the hedge. World 5 tested only the identity layout (0.08) and stalled at 0.44. Worlds 3 and 4 never split and ended near 0.2.

changes.change: Listed the harmful refinements to avoid, and the near-neutral ones to try in rounds 3-4.
changes.evidence: 1 PPO epoch: 0.40 vs 0.79 (world 2), 0.08 vs 0.80 (world 6), 0.31 vs 0.82 (world 7). A third residual block or a wider trunk lowered scores in 5 worlds. n_envs 64 scored 0 in worlds 1 and 5. Gamma 0.97 hurt in worlds 5 and 6. Entropy, 16 minibatches, lr 3e-3 and 3 epochs gave 0.88-0.94.

changes.change: Default ent_coef raised from 0.002 to 0.005.
changes.evidence: Raising entropy helped in world 2 (0.943 vs 0.912), world 7 (0.90 vs 0.82 at 0.01) and world 5 (0.44 vs 0.41). It was neutral in world 1 (0.83 vs 0.88).

changes.change: All-zero fallback: combine a few hedges (obs symmetries, LayerNorm, global context, dilation) instead of widening layouts. Added a cap on r and the update-count check.
changes.evidence: World 3 escaped only with such a combination (0.15-0.23). Three world-3 candidates near r≈2 were invalid because the budget allowed fewer than 4 updates.

changes.change: Shortened the evidence and process text and removed the duplicated 'How the program is used' section.
